A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIND3D by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation scores, timing measurements, robustness experiments, and qualitative results in the main paper and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation experiments and adds a training-data scaling study, annotation-quality audit, and qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The SAM/Gemini annotation pipeline, PT3 backbone, four-layer projection head, pooled contrastive objective, and cosine-similarity segmentation rule are retained. The shortened architecture description and revised annotation counts do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v2 adds qualitative evaluation on PartObjaverse-Tiny, including complex characters and imaginary animals, and removes the explicit DALL-E-generated capybara reconstruction example. The principal quantitative benchmarks remain: ShapeNetPart-V2 is the renamed Objaverse-ShapeNetPart collection, still containing 32 objects from 16 categories.

E2.justification: The principal baseline roster remains unchanged. However, v2 removes the PointNeXt comparison on rotated ShapeNet-Part and the reported PartDistill comparison on PartNet-E, while adding both methods to the timing comparison in Table 1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a training-category sweep spanning 16 to 761 categories and manual inspection of 50 randomly sampled annotated objects. The reported annotation volume changes from 1.5 million to 2.1 million, without establishing that existing benchmark experiments were rerun. Existing mIoU definitions, benchmark subset sizes, training split, and 80-epoch schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new scaling study directly tests generalization against training-category diversity, which v1 left as future work. The appendix adds an annotation-quality audit and examines partial or incorrect labels through successful and unsuccessful examples. Existing prompt, rotation, domain-shift, and model-failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new scaling curve and annotation-quality percentage remain point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds the scaling curve, a finding that 76% of 50 inspected objects have high-quality annotations, new qualitative predictions, and PointNeXt/PartDistill timings. Most benchmark scores are unchanged; v1 Tables 4-6 match v2 Tables 5-7 numerically. Removed entries include PointNeXt's rotated ShapeNet-Part score of 32.18 and PartDistill's cited PartNet-E score of 39.9. The annotation inventory also changes from 1.5 million to 2.1 million.

T1.justification: The point-feature formulation and contrastive-loss equation are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; the added scaling and label-noise explanations are empirical or conceptual.

C1.justification: v2 makes data scarcity and scaling central contributions, claims the first scaling study for 3D part segmentation, and explicitly claims the first model combining open-world, cross-category, part-level, feed-forward inference. It replaces the earlier approximately threefold performance headline with '260% improvement' and adds prominent annotation-diversity and benchmark-size claims.

C2.justification: v1 proposes investigating scaling as future work; v2 interprets its new experiment as showing that data scale and object diversity drive generalization. The appendix newly argues that imperfect annotations still provide semantic supervision and that inconsistent errors can be smoothed out across many examples. The geometric-resolution and symmetry limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes substantial implementation documentation, including serialization choices, 1024-point attention blocks, positional encoding, and nearest-neighbor feature assignment to discarded points. It also removes explicit subset-index/rotation-file locations and details about holding out visually similar categories and all benchmark instances. Core training hyperparameters and Gemini prompts remain; v2 additionally specifies Trellis for photographic reconstructions.

R1.justification: The related-work taxonomy and principal comparisons remain. v2 adds SATR, ImageNetV2, Trellis, and SAMPart3D references, removes several architecture/background references and MCC, and strengthens its contrast with dataset-specific customization. ImageNetV2 supplies a new explicit analogy for the renamed benchmark.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around data scale. Architecture exposition is compressed, experimental discussion is reorganized by benchmark and comparison type, and supplementary sections are expanded and reordered. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds a benchmark visualization, scaling plot, capability/timing table, and extensive annotation and prediction galleries. It reorganizes benchmark tables, promotes existing appendix results into the main text, merges the previous robustness figures, and redraws qualitative comparisons. Existing Gemini-prompt figures are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The scaling experiment and annotation-quality audit provide useful evidence absent from v1, while main-text comparisons using both prompt formats make baseline strengths more visible. These gains are limited by lost reproducibility details and overstated headline arithmetic: v2 Table 2 reports 26.21 versus 10.27 mIoU on unseen categories, approximately a 155% increase rather than the claimed 260%. Overall, empirical support improves modestly, without improved underlying benchmark scores.
